clips.title: The story
paras: In the Stonetalon Mountains, pridewing venom has become a threat to the uneasy peace. Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim from Theramore that orc assassins gather the poison for covert raids. Astranaar's Sentinels send scouts south to claim the venom sacs first.

The Alliance and Horde have not declared open war across northern Kalimdor, but their peace is fragile. Skirmishes break out beneath the forest canopy, and quiet attacks take the place of full armies. Sentinel commanders in Astranaar watch for enemy movements, knowing a careless moment could put their sanctuary at risk.

Shindrell reports an unconfirmed claim from contacts in Theramore about activity in the crags of Stonetalon. Orcish stalkers are said to gather venom from wild pridewings around Mirkfallon Lake and coat their blades for deadly ambushes against Alliance forces. Shindrell Swiftfire sends champions to kill the beasts and claim their venom sacs before Horde agents can reach them.

Shindrell Swiftfire regrets ordering the deaths of native beasts. Night elves revere Kalimdor's wilderness, and the creatures had no part in choosing this war. Yet Astranaar's defenders cannot let an enemy gather poison for lethal attacks, even at the cost of the beasts' lives.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: We are not in open war with the Horde, but our peace is fragile. We often find their agents moving against us, but they do so covertly.

One such advance was revealed to us from hidden sources in Theramore, claiming that the orcs collect venom from the pridewings near Mirkfallon Lake, in the Stonetalon Mountains to the south. Orc assassins then use the venom on their secret death raids against the Alliance!
If this is true, then we must stop them, friend. We must deny them their source of venom.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Do you have the pridewing venom sacs, friend? We cannot allow the orcs to use the beasts' poisons against us!

clips.title: Completion
paras: Thank you, friend. It saddens me to order the slaughter of creatures who may not willingly aid our enemies, yet it is my duty to do so.
Your heart might weep for the pridewings you slew, my friend, but may your heart then swell in knowing that your allies are safe from the pridewings' venom.
